Modern.brandNameRationale: Two words. Good Office names the operational backbone every business actually depends on: a good office function. The brand puts the unglamorous work in the brand position. Warm, plain, immediately legible.
Modern.industrySummary: Modern B2B services is a category serving companies that have grown past in-house generalist support and aren't ready for the giant managed-services vendors. The customer is design-literate and tired of stale enterprise vendors.
Modern.competitorLandscape: Eden (edenworkplace.com) holds the modern workplace-services peer position. Managed by Q (managedbyq.com), now part of WeWork, was a reference. Vinco (myvinco.com) sits in the operations-platform tier. We sit closer to Eden in posture, with sharper brand work.
Modern.positioningStatement: A modern B2B services firm for companies that have grown past their first ops hire.

targetAudience.primary: 28 to 50. Founders, COOs, and Heads of People at companies of 50 to 500 people. They've grown past their first ops hire and need a partner that handles the operational backbone.

dos: Speak to the founder, not the procurement department

Modern.logoDirection: A wordmark only. GOOD OFFICE in a tight modern grotesk, all caps, two words on one line. A small geometric mark, two thin parallel lines suggesting a desk edge, used as the favicon and on every service report.

typography.secondary: GT America Mono for service specs and prices
typography.rationale: One family. The mono carries the service data. The regular carries the brand.

Luxury.brandNameRationale: Two words. The Bureau is the older European word for a quiet firm that handles the unglamorous business of running a household, an office, or an estate. The definite article makes it an institution. The whole name reads as a heritage services firm that has been operating quietly for decades.
Luxury.story: The Bureau began as a small operations practice serving a few significant family offices and private businesses. The current generation has stayed at the same address. The client list has stayed small. Some clients have been with The Bureau across multiple businesses.
Luxury.industrySummary: Top end B2B services have been moving toward larger managed-services firms and bigger marketing. There's a parallel market for small principal-led firms providing back-office, operations, and concierge work to a small set of clients across decades.
Luxury.competitorLandscape: Bain Capital's Sankaty operations services (sankaty.com) holds the institutional peer position. Quincy (heyquincy.com) sits in the modern peer middle. The traditional family-office back-office firms hold the heritage peer position. We sit smaller and quieter than all of them.
Luxury.positioningStatement: A small heritage services firm for businesses and family offices that prefer their operations handled quietly.

targetAudience.primary: Family office principals, founders of long-running private businesses, and trustees of foundations. They value the discretion above all.

dos: Speak in the language of the discipline
Send paper letters where the situation warrants

Luxury.logoDirection: A classical serif wordmark with elegant ligatures. A small hand-drawn folder hallmark, two thin lines suggesting a folio, used on letterhead, the brass plaque outside the office, and the wax seal of every paper letter.

Minimal.brandNameRationale: Single word. Done is the outcome the customer is paying for. The brand names the result, not the work, in one syllable. Plain, direct, and slightly satisfying.
Minimal.industrySummary: Most B2B services brands have elaborate names suggesting partnership, transformation, or scale. There's an opening for one that strips it back to the outcome: the task is done. Said as such.
Minimal.competitorLandscape: Most B2B services brands fail this purity test. The closest peers in spirit are some Japanese back-office services and certain Scandinavian operations firms.
Minimal.positioningStatement: A back-office services firm that closes tickets and sends a one-line confirmation.

targetAudience.primary: Founders and small-business owners who want operational tasks handled and don't want a relationship with the vendor. They want the task done, the receipt, and silence.

dos: Confirm the task in one line

typography.rationale: One face. The intake, the confirmation, and the invoice all carry the same wordmark.

Corporate.brandNameRationale: Two surnames joined by an ampersand. Marsh is short and earthy; Hayes is grounded and slightly Welsh. The uneven rhythm (one short syllable, one short syllable but different texture) makes the pair feel like a real, slightly mismatched partnership rather than a typed-up corporate name.
Corporate.industrySummary: Enterprise operations services is a B2B category serving large corporates that outsource finance, HR, IT, and procurement back-office functions. The category is dominated by the global giants and a few regional players. Buyers want partners with operating discipline and clean reporting.
Corporate.competitorLandscape: Accenture (accenture.com) is the institutional giant. Cognizant (cognizant.com) holds the same tier. Genpact (genpact.com) is the operations-led peer. We sit smaller and more focused on the mid-market enterprise client.
Corporate.positioningStatement: Operations services for mid-market enterprises that have outgrown their first wave of outsourcing.
Corporate.positioningRationale: Mid-market enterprises want operations partners with the discipline of the giants and the responsiveness of a smaller firm. We sit between them.

Creative.brandNameRationale: Two words. The Inbox names the universal hellscape of modern professional life. The brand puts the customer's actual pain in the brand position. Loud, warm, and immediately legible.
Creative.manifesto: Most B2B services brands sell partnership, transformation, and scale. We made The Inbox because the truth about running a business is that most of the work is the inbox. The unread messages. The follow-ups. The 'just circling back'. The brand is for the people whose inbox is bigger than their team, and for the small firms that exist to make it smaller.
Creative.industrySummary: B2B services branding has been polished, scale-led, and slightly intimidating. There's room for a brand that's warm, character-driven, sticker-friendly, and serious about the actual quiet work of clearing the inbox.
Creative.competitorLandscape: Magic (getmagic.com) does playful B2B assistance. Athena (athenago.com) holds the modern executive-assistant peer position. Time etc (timeetc.com) sits in the assistant-services middle. We sit warmer than any of them.
Creative.positioningStatement: A small services firm that lives in the inbox so the founder doesn't have to.

targetAudience.primary: 30 to 50. Founders, executives, and small-business owners whose inbox is too full. They want a partner who lives in the inbox and clears it daily.

dos: Quote the worst subject line of the week
Talk like the assistant who has the inbox open
donts: Run a 'future of work' content campaign

Creative.logoDirection: A wordmark in a punchy display serif with the I of INBOX stylized as a small envelope flap. Standalone envelope-flap icon for stickers, social profiles, and the back of every onboarding folder.

customSections.body: Not a productivity software brand. Not a 'future of work' brand. Not afraid of red. Not too cool to admit the inbox is the problem.

customSections.body: An onboarding folder that's actually one short doc. Stickers in every welcome envelope. A weekly newsletter that's mostly funny subject lines. A merch line of two tees that say THE INBOX across the back.
